title: DevExp standup blitz notes — Jul 8 2026
content:
Context and purpose:
This was a short, high-velocity standup ("blitz" format) to sync SDK + quickstarts + sample repos after the sprint cutover. Focus: unblock the 1.0 quickstart landing, decide on one onboarding flow for new users, and triage the remaining sample spec gaps. Meeting ran ~25 minutes (no slides) — mostly voice and shared screen.

Attendees (oncall + optional):
- Maya (owner) — running notes
- Jonah — SDK lead
- Priya — Docs/content + QA
- Luis — Samples and examples
- Samir — Console / quickstart integration
- Alexis (joined briefly) — Solutions engineer

Quick hits / status
- SDK RC: Jonah reports the RC for 1.2.0 has flaky Windows CI on embedding tests (timeout flake). Repro locally on WSL; not seen on Linux. PR linked above.
- Quickstarts: Two flows under consideration: "CLI-first" vs "SDK-tokens-first". Consensus leaned toward CLI-first for initial drop (easier to demo streaming + function calls). Need final doc update.
- Samples: Luis finished the simple-chat sample but the multi-turn reranking example is missing corpus and eval script. Blocking: sample-data license question (legal).
- Console: Samir enabled a short-lived demo token flow for internal previews. Need to rotate token and add telemetry to avoid noise in cost dashboards.

Decisions made (fast):
1) Ship CLI-first quickstart as the canonical onboarding flow for the 1.0 doc bundle. Rationale: minimal friction for new devs, demonstrates streaming & function-calling end-to-end.
2) Defer the SDK-auth-first flow to a separate "advanced onboarding" page (post-launch).
3) For Windows CI flake, run an isolated job that retries once and collects enhanced logs; if flake persists, bisect the change set.

Open blockers / risks
- Legal review required on sample dataset (multi-turn reranker). Luis flagged CC-BY upstream but legal wants provenance and business-use okay. Blocker ID: JIRA-ENG-9276.
- Docs: The CLI quickstart still references the old "--model=redwood-001" flag; needs to be updated to new model spec and include region fallback example.
- Telemetry: Demo tokens are inflating internal cost dashboard numbers; Samir to add a tag so we can filter.

Action items (owner — due):
- Jonah — add retry wrapper for flaky Windows CI job + attach full debug logs to PR #412 (due: 2026-07-10).
- Priya — update CLI quickstart page: replace model flag, add region fallback snippet, and add a 60-second troubleshooting section (due: 2026-07-12).
- Luis — submit legal ticket with sample data provenance + alternative synthetic dataset if legal rejects CC-BY. Ping legal by EOD (due: 2026-07-09).
- Samir — rotate internal demo token and add "demo:true" telemetry tag to calls so dashboards can exclude them (due: 2026-07-09).
- Maya — consolidate standup notes into quick-run handoff doc and create a follow-up async thread in #devexp-standups (due: 2026-07-09).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (fragmented)
- Consider adding a short video (60–90s) that walks through CLI-first quickstart + captureboard recording for marketing demo. Might reduce support questions.
- Could we create a small automated smoke test that runs the quickstart end-to-end using ephemeral tokens? If yes, that would catch region fallback regressions.
- Flag: function-calling sample needs a tiny schema example and a note on deterministic vs. stochastic outputs — Priya to draft language.

Follow-ups and async work
- Priya to post a docs diff in the #docs-review channel once drafted. Request a quick eyeball from Solutions (Alexis) before merging.
- Luis to attach sample data alternatives to JIRA-ENG-9276 and @legal in Slack for faster triage.
- Jonah to post CI artifacts link in PR and summarize any binary dependency changes affecting Windows.

Meeting fragments (verbatim lines captured quickly)
- "CLI-first gets more eyeballs; easy to script into a workshop." — Alexis
- "If legal blocks, we can generate a synthetic lorem-style convo set in <1 day." — Luis
- "We need to standardize the quickstart exit criteria — 'bot replies are coherent' is too fuzzy." — Priya

Parking lot (defer to next deep-dive)
- Cross-team playbook: how to do quick demo tokens safely across infra (SRE + Console).
- Canonical sample metrics: add a tiny CI eval that confirms samples run within latency & cost budgets.

Attachments / links mentioned during the meeting
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/412
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-9276 (samples legal)
- Slack thread: #devexp-standups: thread ts 1720529400.000100 (internal)

Tone / retrospective blip
- Fast, actionable standup worked well for this set of decisions. We should repeat "blitz" format for short pre-launch syncs (<=30m). For larger cross-team topics, keep the longer meeting slot.

If you read nothing else — TL;DR:
- Ship CLI-first quickstart (Priya to update docs).
- Jonah fixes Windows CI flake and posts logs to PR #412.
- Luis to resolve sample licensing with legal quickly or provide synthetic fallback.

-- Maya
(putting this in drive for traceability; will update after Priya's doc diff lands)
